title: Season eight of Netflix’s ‘Drive to Survive’ to be shown on Apple TV in the U.S.
content:
In a shocking move, Apple TV and Netflix are collaborating with each other this Formula 1 season, starting with the launch of “Drive to Survive” Season 8 on Friday.

The behind-the-scenes docuseries will be available on Apple TV for the U.S. audience and globally on Netflix, marking the first time ever that it has not been solely shown on Netflix. In turn, Netflix will air Apple TV’s Canadian Grand Prix live coverage to the U.S. audience. Netflix has experimented with the F1 space before beyond “Drive to Survive,” with the Netflix Cup in Nov. 2023, where four golfers and four F1 drivers teamed up for the eight-hole competition.

It is a significant moment for the sport as it continues to expand its reach with an ever-growing fanbase. “Drive to Survive” is one of the reasons F1’s stateside popularity boomed after the COVID-19 pandemic, at a time when sporting events were scarce and lockdowns occurred worldwide. The docuseries is known for telling the human stories behind the sport and giving fans a look behind-the-scenes of how some of the previous year’s biggest moments played out.

But to be able to watch the racing product, fans had to go to other platforms. ESPN secured the U.S. broadcasting rights in 2018, but its deal expired last year and other companies began circling. On the heels of the successful F1 movie, which was developed by Apple Studios, it was announced in October 2025 that Apple officially would be the exclusive U.S. broadcaster, agreeing a deal in the $120 million to $150 million per year range.

The agreement marked a significant shift in F1’s broadcasting philosophy. The sport had long used traditional broadcasting partners, and moving to a streaming giant like Apple does come with some risk. F1’s leaders, though, are confident this move will help grow the sport more.

Apple TV will feature a comprehensive package with its F1 viewing experience, covering all track sessions this season. It is anticipated that F1’s presence will expand to a few other Apple products. For example, on the Apple Maps view of Melbourne’s Albert Park circuit, the track outline, turn numbers and F1 cars can be seen.
